name: Dak Nong
provinceNote: National Assembly Resolution 202/2025/QH15 merged Dak Nong, Binh Thuan, and former Lam Dong into a new Lam Dong province from 12 Jun 2025, with the administrative center at Da Lat. Visitor sites still print Dak Nong on their pages.
dotReason: Worth a geopark loop from the highlands
summary: A highland geopark in the Central Highlands, with wide waterfalls, lake islands and volcanic lava tubes. See the Dray Sap falls on the Serepok River, take a boat on Ta Dung lake, and eat bamboo-tube rice with grilled meat. A two- or three-day road trip by car or motorbike suits nature lovers.
fee: No single province ticket. Gate prices are Check on arrival.
getThere: Fly to Buon Ma Thuot, then the road to Gia Nghia. Dak Nong has no airport.
bestMonths: January to early April for the roads; May to October for fuller falls
seoTitle: Dak Nong travel guide — Dray Sap and the island lake
seoDescription: Dray Sap is about 100 metres wide on the Serepok, about 110 km from Gia Nghia. Ta Dung’s islands sit about 45 km the other way. Fly to Buon Ma Thuot.
intro: Stand where the Serepok drops in one wide sheet through primary forest. Dray Sap is about 100 metres across and about 12 metres down, in Dak Sor, Krong No, about 110 km from Gia Nghia, with Gia Long and Trinh Nu falls in the same cluster. Give it a day of its own. It is not a stop you add after a Ta Dung morning.

Ta Dung is the other picture: the Dong Nai 3 reservoir at Dak Som and Dak Plao, in Dak Glong, with dozens of wooded islands, the highlands’ own Ha Long Bay. The lake is about 45 km southeast of Gia Nghia on QL28. Entry to the park is free; boats and lakeside resorts sell their own tickets. Sleep in Dak Som when the boat is the morning and the cool air is half the point.

Gia Nghia sits where National Highway 14 meets National Highway 28. Lieng Nung, a 35-metre fall inside a hexagonal basalt vault, is about 9 km out on QL28. EXPLORASOUND, on Dak Nur hill, is Vietnam’s first sound museum. The Dak Kar lithophone hall, about 9 km toward Da Lat in Dak Nia, keeps stones nearly 3,000 years old. Buon Buor, about 90 km toward Dak Lak, is an Ede longhouse village on the Serepok. Evenings in town are dinner and an early night.

Stay if you will hire a car or a motorbike and accept the distances. Fly into Buon Ma Thuot when the Serepok is the plan, or into Lien Khuong, near Da Lat, when Ta Dung and the cool hills are one trip. The mistakes are stacking Krong No and the lake into the same morning, and walking into a lava tube without an authorized guide: Krong No banned self-guided entry after deaths. C9, near Chu Bluk, is a 217-metre tube with free entry; settle the guide’s fee before you go in.
gettingAround: Dak Nong has no airport of its own. How far Buon Ma Thuot is from Gia Nghia depends on who is counting: the provincial handbook says about 125 km, Bao Lam Dong about 135 km, and Vexere about 120 km and two hours for the airport limousine. One limousine line, Hoang Kim, has listed 150,000 VND; night buses run higher. From Ho Chi Minh City it is about 250 km and about six hours by bus, for about 150,000–200,000 VND. Gia Nghia to Da Lat is about 180 km and four to four and a half hours. Ta Dung is about 45 km southeast on QL28, and Dray Sap about 110 km away in Krong No. For more than one stop, hire a car or a motorbike and line it up before you arrive.

stayAreas.name: Gia Nghia
stayAreas.summary: Town hotels and guesthouses on the highway crossroads, for Lieng Nung, the sound museum, and the long drives to Krong No.

stayAreas.name: Ta Dung lakeshore
stayAreas.summary: Lodges and homestays in Dak Som when the boat morning matters more than being in town.

eat: Com lam, sticky rice cooked in bamboo, is the meal at M'Nong and Ma gatherings, eaten with grilled meat. Grilled catfish from the Serepok is the specialty through Krong No and Cu Jut. Ruou can is a shared jar at a ceremony.

Robusta grows on the basalt, and coffee and pepper farms sit around Quang Tan and Dak R'tih in Tuy Duc; Arabica and Culi are grown too. Dak R'Mang, in Dak Glong, holds a Sunday market with Hmong traders, textiles, thang co, and corn wine.
interestsBody: Dray Sap is the wide Serepok cascade, about 100 metres across and about 12 metres down, about 110 km from Gia Nghia.
Ta Dung is the island reservoir, about 45 km southeast on QL28. The park is free to enter; boats and resorts sell their own tickets.
Krong No’s lava tubes are a guided visit only. C9 is a free, 217-metre tube; the guide is a separate arrangement.
EXPLORASOUND and the Dak Kar lithophones are short stops from Gia Nghia. Buon Buor is the Ede longhouse village, about 90 km toward Dak Lak.

interestGroups.summary: The wide cascade on the Serepok, then the island lake, the lawful caves, and the short stops out of Gia Nghia.

cards.title: Dray Sap Waterfall
cards.summary: A wide Serepok cascade in primary forest, about 100 metres across and about 12 metres down. About 110 km from Gia Nghia.

blocks.heading: The wide sheet
paragraphs: Dray Sap spreads about 100 metres across and drops about 12 metres through primary forest. The eco-site is in Dak Sor, Krong No, about 110 km from Gia Nghia, with Gia Long and Trinh Nu falls in the same cluster. Listings give 07:30–18:00 for the cluster; there is no official ticket page.

blocks.heading: Ta Dung
paragraphs: Ta Dung is the Dong Nai 3 reservoir at Dak Som and Dak Plao, about 45 km southeast of Gia Nghia on QL28. Its wooded islands are why people call it the highlands’ Ha Long Bay. Entry to the park is free; boats and resorts sell their own tickets. Granite waterfall sits in the same park. Do not treat the lake as a same-day add-on from Da Lat.

blocks.heading: Lawful caves only
paragraphs: Krong No banned self-guided entry to the lava tubes, C7 included, after deaths. Go with an authorized guide. C9, also called Hang Doi, near Chu Bluk, is a 217-metre tube with free entry; settle the guide’s fee before you go in. Nam Kar is a roadside scoria cone on QL28 between Gia Nghia and Krong No.

blocks.heading: Sound, stone, and the longhouse
paragraphs: EXPLORASOUND, on Dak Nur hill in Gia Nghia, is Vietnam’s first sound museum. The Dak Kar lithophone hall is about 9 km from central Gia Nghia on QL28 toward Da Lat, in Dak Nia, and its stones are nearly 3,000 years old. Buon Buor, in Tam Thang, Cu Jut, is about 90 km toward Dak Lak: Ede longhouses, weaving, and gongs on the Serepok. Lieng Nung, about 9 km from Gia Nghia, is the 35-metre fall inside a basalt vault.

body: One hired car or motorbike covers the loop. Dray Sap and Ta Dung are different days. Evenings in Gia Nghia are quiet: this is festival and gong country, not a bar street.

season.label: Dry roads, fuller falls
season.note: January to early April is the easy window, with dry roads and coffee blossom in March. Golden shower trees flower in May and June. From May to October the wet season brings quick showers and fuller waterfalls. Hoi Xuan Lieng Nung is a spring gathering around Gia Nghia with no fixed Gregorian date. Long Tong, the Tay and Nung rice festival in Nam Tan, Krong No, follows the lunar calendar; in 2023 it fell on the 10th day of the first lunar month, 31 January. After heavy rain, ask locally before driving the back roads.

faqs.q: Should you fly into Dak Nong?
faqs.a: Dak Nong has no airport. Fly to Buon Ma Thuot: the provincial handbook puts Gia Nghia about 125 km away, Bao Lam Dong about 135 km, and Vexere about 120 km and two hours by airport limousine. Lien Khuong, near Da Lat, is the other flight when Ta Dung is the plan; Gia Nghia to Da Lat is about 180 km and four to four and a half hours.

faqs.q: Can you walk into the volcanic caves on your own?
faqs.a: No. Krong No banned self-guided entry to the lava tubes, C7 included, after deaths. Go with an authorized guide. C9 is a 217-metre tube with free entry; settle the guide’s fee before you go in.

faqs.q: How many days does the geopark need?
faqs.a: Two days cover Gia Nghia, a short stop such as Lieng Nung, and a Ta Dung boat morning. Add a third for Dray Sap, about 110 km from Gia Nghia, so it is never the same morning as the lake.
